top_news.title: Global partnerships, youth and women crucial for maritime future: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal
top_news.summary: Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal held bilateral meetings with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan on Day 2 of Sagarmanthan. The Great Oceans Dialogue 2026, carrying India's maritime partnerships across the Gulf, Europe and the neighbourhood. He also placed young people and women at the centre of India's maritime journey. With a delegation from the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani), Sarbananda Sonowal discussed Saudi participation in Indian port projects such as Vadhavan and Galathea Bay. The two sides also discussed cooperation in shipbuilding, seafarer training and resilient supply chains. Saudi Arabia expressed their interest in investing in India's port projects and in the Maritime Development Fund (MDF). With Flemish Minister for Mobility, Public Works, Ports and Sport, Annick De Ridder, Sonowal proposed exploring a green shipping corridor linking Indian ports with Antwerp-Bruges. Both sides discussed green fuels, smart port technology, and dredging. VOC Port has signed an agreement with the Port of Antwerp for training and capacity building in green shipping and green fuel. With Lyonpo Chandra Bahadur Gurung, Minister of Infrastructure and Transport of Bhutan, Sonowal highlighted National Waterway-2 and the Jogighopa terminal as Bhutan's gateway to global trade. The ministers discussed the potential of the Manas and Sankosh rivers, and the connectivity with the national waterways for improved cargo movement. Both ministers discussed maritime training for Bhutanese youth at the Centre of Excellence in Dibrugarh, which is being developed. Our talks with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan show how India's maritime partnerships are growing across regions, said Sarbananda Sonowal. With Saudi Arabia, we are exploring investment in ports, shipbuilding and resilient supply chains. With Belgium, we are working towards a green shipping corridor and smarter ports. With Bhutan, we are opening the Brahmaputra as a gateway for our neighbour to reach global markets and build skills for its youth. top_news.title: Microsoft reacts to US immigration crackdown while Trump honours Nadella
top_news.summary: Microsoft on Thursday (local time) responded to the Trump administration's immigration crackdown after being suspended from the Permanent Labour Certification Program, while US President Donald Trump honoured Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Microsoft, in its response, said it believes in the "strength and talent of the American workforce" and highlighted that the vast majority of its US employees are Americans. The statement came as Trump praised Nadella for his leadership and role in transforming Microsoft. On recent immigration questions, Microsoft issued a statement saying, "We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce. That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans." "We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people," the company further said. Microsoft said the remaining H-1B filings for new employees involved people who were already legally present in the United States and chose to join the company. "They are not new arrivals to our country," it said, adding that these employees accounted for only one per cent of Microsoft's US workforce. The company said it only files H-1B petitions for employees who meet the "rigorous standards" of the visa category and disputed any suggestion that its foreign workers were being paid less than other employees. "We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work," Microsoft said. "Microsoft succeeds as a global technology leader by developing the world's best technology workforce. We do this by strengthening this country's talent pipeline, hiring American workers, and attracting the best talent from around the world," it added. articles.title: Global partnerships, youth and women crucial for maritime future: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal
articles.summary: Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal held bilateral meetings with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan on Day 2 of Sagarmanthan. The Great Oceans Dialogue 2026, carrying India's maritime partnerships across the Gulf, Europe and the neighbourhood. He also placed young people and women at the centre of India's maritime journey. With a delegation from the Saudi Ports Authority (Mawani), Sarbananda Sonowal discussed Saudi participation in Indian port projects such as Vadhavan and Galathea Bay. The two sides also discussed cooperation in shipbuilding, seafarer training and resilient supply chains. Saudi Arabia expressed their interest in investing in India's port projects and in the Maritime Development Fund (MDF). With Flemish Minister for Mobility, Public Works, Ports and Sport, Annick De Ridder, Sonowal proposed exploring a green shipping corridor linking Indian ports with Antwerp-Bruges. Both sides discussed green fuels, smart port technology, and dredging. VOC Port has signed an agreement with the Port of Antwerp for training and capacity building in green shipping and green fuel. With Lyonpo Chandra Bahadur Gurung, Minister of Infrastructure and Transport of Bhutan, Sonowal highlighted National Waterway-2 and the Jogighopa terminal as Bhutan's gateway to global trade. The ministers discussed the potential of the Manas and Sankosh rivers, and the connectivity with the national waterways for improved cargo movement. Both ministers discussed maritime training for Bhutanese youth at the Centre of Excellence in Dibrugarh, which is being developed. Our talks with Saudi Arabia, Belgium and Bhutan show how India's maritime partnerships are growing across regions, said Sarbananda Sonowal. With Saudi Arabia, we are exploring investment in ports, shipbuilding and resilient supply chains. With Belgium, we are working towards a green shipping corridor and smarter ports. With Bhutan, we are opening the Brahmaputra as a gateway for our neighbour to reach global markets and build skills for its youth. articles.title: Microsoft reacts to US immigration crackdown while Trump honours Nadella
articles.summary: Microsoft on Thursday (local time) responded to the Trump administration's immigration crackdown after being suspended from the Permanent Labour Certification Program, while US President Donald Trump honoured Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Microsoft, in its response, said it believes in the "strength and talent of the American workforce" and highlighted that the vast majority of its US employees are Americans. The statement came as Trump praised Nadella for his leadership and role in transforming Microsoft. On recent immigration questions, Microsoft issued a statement saying, "We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce. That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans." "We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people," the company further said. Microsoft said the remaining H-1B filings for new employees involved people who were already legally present in the United States and chose to join the company. "They are not new arrivals to our country," it said, adding that these employees accounted for only one per cent of Microsoft's US workforce. The company said it only files H-1B petitions for employees who meet the "rigorous standards" of the visa category and disputed any suggestion that its foreign workers were being paid less than other employees. "We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work," Microsoft said. "Microsoft succeeds as a global technology leader by developing the world's best technology workforce. We do this by strengthening this country's talent pipeline, hiring American workers, and attracting the best talent from around the world," it added.
